title: MPIA Request Regarding Use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) (Baltimore Police Department)

communications.subject: Maryland Public Information Act Request: MPIA Request Regarding Use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) (Baltimore Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Maryland Public Information Act, I am hereby requesting access to the records listed below and held by the Baltimore Police Department.

1)	Any policies, procedures, protocols, and/or written guidance for the use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) by Baltimore Police Department. This request includes, but is not limited to policies setting forth permitted and prohibited uses for ALPRs and rules regarding who may and may not use this technology.

2)	Information about which people and agencies have access to images, videos, and raw data sets generated by ALPR systems monitored or maintained by Baltimore Police Department, under what circumstances these individuals have access to the above-mentioned data, and what information must be entered about any data requests. The list of agencies includes, but is not limited to, parking and traffic enforcement agencies, and other law enforcement agencies.

3)	Policies, procedures and information regarding Baltimore Police Department data retention and data purging practices for ALPR systems, including  Baltimore Police Department policies regarding handling images, videos, and raw data sets.

4)	Information about Baltimore Police Department audits or other procedures used to assure compliance with the above requirements.

5)	Information regarding the training that Baltimore Police Department personnel must undergo to use ALPRs, if any.

6)	ALPR training materials provided to Baltimore Police Department.

7)	Product and user manuals for all ALPR software and hardware possessed or used by Baltimore Police Department.

8)	The name of all ALPR vendors, ALPR software systems, and ALPR hardware currently used by Baltimore Police Department or by third party who make the information available to Baltimore Police Department. Hardware includes fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile devices. Software systems include optical character recognition and artificial intelligence capabilities.

9)	Description of how targets (aka “hot lists”) are shared with ALPR systems and monitored, including the sources for these data feeds.

10)	A list and map of locations where fixed-location ALPRs are currently located within Baltimore Police Department’s jurisdiction.

11)	The number of ALPR devices operated by the agency for the following categories: fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile ALPRs.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, please disclose total charges in advance of fulfilling the request. Alternatively, please consider waiving any fees, pursuant to § 4-206(e)(2)(ii) of the General Provisions Article, as this request is on behalf of individuals served by the Maryland Office of the Public Defender, a state government agency, which solely serves indigent citizens of Maryland. As a result, my request for the above-listed public records is in the public interest. I would prefer the request be filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available, or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jeff Gilleran
Chief Attorney
Forensics Division
Office of the Public Defender
6 St. Paul St., Suite 1508
Baltimore, MD 21202
(410) 804-7107
jeffrey.gilleran@maryland.gov

All arrest and booking records, with booking photographs where you keep them, from January 1, 2015 (or as far back as your system retains) to the present, with name, date of birth, booking or arrest date, charges and release date, as a CSV or spreadsheet export sent by reply.

If that's a large lift, the last five years, or whatever portion you can provide at no cost, would be wonderful. If any fee would apply, please let us know first rather than starting the work. If any part can't be shared, the rest would still help.

Thank you so much for your time and help.

All the best

Attached is the report I could find that most closely matches your request. I should note that data prior to 2022 was converted from another system into our current management system. So, there may be issues with any data prior to 2022. If you feel I missed something from your request or have additional questions, you can email me directly at churtado@co.tuolumne.ca.us.

communications.subject: The Kansas Open Records Act Request: Beale Infrastructure De Soto data center ("Project Pilot") records (City Of De Soto)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the The Kansas Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records of your agency, including records held by its elected or appointed officials, board members, staff, engineers, contractors, and attorneys, created or received from January 1, 2024 through the date of this request.

"The Project" means the data center campus proposed by Beale Infrastructure or any affiliate, developer, or landowner on its behalf in the City of De Soto, south of K-10 near the former Sunflower Army Ammunition Plant site (103rd Street / Edgerton Road area), including any version of it called "Project Pilot" or any other code name, and any other data center proposal your agency received in the same period.

1. Applications and requests concerning the Project, including rezoning, plat, site plan, and water, wastewater, or main-extension service requests, and your agency's responses, including staff reports and will-serve or availability letters.

2. Agreements and drafts concerning the Project, including development, economic development, Industrial Revenue Bond, payment-in-lieu-of-taxes (PILOT), tax abatement, franchise, water or wastewater service, infrastructure, cost-sharing, benefit-area, and reimbursement agreements; letters of intent; term sheets; memoranda of understanding; and any nondisclosure or confidentiality agreements, including any provision treating water usage as confidential.

3. Water and wastewater demand or usage projections (average day, maximum day, peak hour, fill and commissioning volumes), hydraulic modeling, capacity studies, and infrastructure cost estimates for the Project.

4. Agendas, packets, minutes, presentations, and resolutions of your governing body, board, or planning commission referencing the Project or data centers, including any rule, rate, or policy changes for large water users.

5. Correspondence, including emails and attachments, concerning the Project between your agency and any of: Beale Infrastructure or its affiliates, consultants, engineers, attorneys, or lobbyists; the City of De Soto; Johnson County Rural Water District No. 7; Johnson County Water District No. 1 (WaterOne); any wholesale water supplier; Evergy; the Kansas Department of Health and Environment; or Johnson County.

6. Internal emails among your agency's officials, board or council members, administrator or general manager, attorney, and planning, economic development, engineering, or utility staff that reference "data center," "Beale," or "Pilot."

To limit cost, searches for items 5 and 6 may exclude newsletters, automated notifications, and duplicate copies of the same message within a thread.

Please provide records in native electronic format (emails with attachments).

If any record is withheld in whole or part, please release all reasonably segregable portions (K.S.A. 45-221(d)) and provide a written statement of the specific statutory provision relied on for each withholding (K.S.A. 45-218(d)).

If fees will exceed $25 or the request will take more than one hour of staff time, please send an itemized estimate before starting work so I can narrow or phase the request. 
If phased, please process items 2 and 3 first.

I am a Kansas resident.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jonathan Modisett

Good afternoon,

We have reviewed your records request related to the Beale data center project and have preliminarily determined that the cost of staff time required to gather, review, and produce the responsive records will likely exceed $200, primarily due to the request for correspondence. As required by the Kansas Open Records Act (KORA), we are reaching out to explore opportunities to reduce costs or narrow the scope of the request.

We believe that many, if not most, of the records requested under Sections 1–3 may already be available as part of previous records requests the City has fulfilled. Additionally, we have previously gathered and reviewed email correspondence related to the Beale project through approximately August 2025. These records can be provided to you free of charge, as the work associated with gathering and reviewing them has already been completed.

I am also able to provide an unredacted copy of the development agreement and its supplements, which I will send to you tomorrow.

In an effort to minimize costs, we would like to offer you the records we currently have available at no charge and suggest that you review them before proceeding with your full request. This would allow you to determine whether the available records meet your needs or whether you would like to narrow or revise your request to obtain additional records.

Should you wish to proceed with your request as originally submitted, we will work to prepare a good-faith estimate of the costs associated with fulfilling it. The primary factor contributing to these costs is the search for general city records and the request for correspondence, as staff must conduct email searches, review the results to determine whether the records are responsive, and evaluate any applicable KORA exemptions, including obtaining legal review as necessary. Our preliminary estimate is that these efforts will result in at least $200-$300 in staff time fees.

Please let me know how you would like to proceed so that we can prepare accordingly.

Thank you,

Edgar Marquez

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: TSA Information Assurance (IA) Handbook
communications.communication:
Dear TSA,

This letter is a formal Freedom of Information Act request for the following record(s):

TSA Information Assurance (IA) Handbook

I request the original electronic record in original electronic format. For all records requested, as part of the record, I also request all record metadata.

See below for important definitions, exclusions, form & format requirements, etc.

Thank you for your assistance in making records of such extreme public interest promptly and maximally available.


### 
Fiat Fiendum FOIA template 
Version 6
###

# Changelog

6: Updated prioritization and form/format clauses; removed additional requests
5.1: Updated 508 provisions to refer to Access Board's final rule, 82 FR 5790, and reference https://www.access-board.gov/ict/ & https://section508.gov .

# FOIA template structure

All content after the version number line above, except for the contact details at the very end, is part of my standard FOIA request template and identical between all of my FOIA requests. The provisions below are generally applicable to all FOIA / Privacy Act requests that I make.

There is one exception: the contact details below my signature at the very bottom (provided by MuckRock) are different for each request. Please use the distinct contact details matching each request, to ensure that your responses are correctly tracked.


The template provisions specify e.g. additional requests relating to my FOIA/PA requests themselves, form and format, timing, redaction & review, rolling updates, § 508 compliance, identity, fee waiver, my identity, and the like. They apply to this request, but are not specific to it.

If anything in the request-specific section above explicitly overrides anything in this template section, the request-specific section controls. If there is any ambiguity about such an override, please ask me for clarification.


The version number above is provided to make it easier for you to process my requests. Since all content (except contact info) below identical version number lines is identical between my requests, you need track only the request-specific portions (at the top) and the latest version of my general provisions.  

Please read each new version carefully, as updates generally contain substantive changes.


## Template version updates

If you receive any FOIA request from me with a newer template version number than any pending prior FOIA requests from me, please replace the template portion of all prior requests with the updated version, treat the update as a clarification of and/or extension to the prior request, and process each updated request accordingly. Do not close the original request or change its request date. If you are permitted by law to refuse to honor such an update, and you choose to exercise that refusal, please process any differences between the new version and the prior version as a new FOIA request in its own right.


# Prioritization

In order to respond in a most expedited manner possible, please prioritize, in order:
a. records already scanned or electronically available
b. records not labelled as classified
c. records requiring the least time and effort to produce
d. in the order listed in paragraph 1 above 

Please produce all records on a daily rolling basis — i.e. on each day that any record is ready to release, release it that day, even if other records (or the accompanying cover / withholding letter) are not yet ready.

In order to expedite rolling production, you are welcome to delay providing the cover / withholding claims letter normally included in each production, provided that the letter is provided within 2 weeks (e.g. so as to cover the last 2 weeks' productions as a batch in one letter). 


# All requests are for the full record, including metadata and prior versions

For all responsive records, I also request:

1. all parts of the record (i.e. no portion of a record with some responsive portion may be considered "non-responsive");
2. all versions of the record, whether or not currently in use;
3. all record metadata, such as dates on which they were drafted, passed, went into effect, withdrawn, or similar events; person(s) / office(s) responsible; authors;  IDs; revision numbers; etc.;
4. a detailed index of all claims of exemption/privilege, regardless of whether the record is claimed to be exempt in whole or in part;
access to inspect the record directly, in its native electronic format; and
5. if any classification applies, mandatory declassification review (MDR) under E.O. 13526, and the result of the MDR, including any declassified records.

"All parts of the record" means that the "record" should be considered to be the most comprehensive record with any responsive portion. For instance:
a) if any portion of an email is responsive, the entire contents of all email thread(s) to which that email belongs is also responsive (including attachments);
b) if a record is part of a larger record, such as a responsive table that is in a chapter of a report, then the entire larger record (e.g. the full report) is responsive, together with any appendices, amendments, etc.;
c) if a record is part of a book, the entire book is responsive;
d) if a record is part of a database, all related database records are responsive; 
etc.

"Related database records" has the technical meaning used in relational database management systems (such as SQL). It recursively includes all directly and indirectly related records (starting with all responsive records, include as responsive the full row of each, and recursively include as responsive all rows for which any responsive record has a foreign key or is referenced by a foreign key), together with the schema for all responsive records.

Items in this part should be prioritized at the same level as the record they apply to.


# Timing

For all requests above, the "cut-off date" is, at the earliest, the date that you conduct the search.

The priority order listed above is only for items that may take extra time to respond to, and must not be taken as blocking response to an otherwise lower priority item that could be released more quickly than a higher priority item that is pending time-intensive search or review.


# FOIA IA notice

Please note that this request is made after the enactment of Public Law No. 114-185, S. 337 (114th), the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016 (FOIA IA). The revised statute, as specified in the FOIA IA, applies to this request. FOIA IA § 6. 

In particular, please note that:
1. you must provide electronic format documents, §§ 552(a)(2) (undesignated preceding text), 552(a)(2)(E) (undesignated following text), 552(a)(3)(B), and 552(a)(3)(C);
2. you may not specify an appeal duration less than 90 days, § 552(a)(6)(C)(A)(i)(III)(aa);
3. you may not withhold any record unless "the agency reasonably foresees that disclosure would harm an interest protected by an exemption described in subsection (b), or disclosure is prohibited by law", § 552(a)(8)(A)(i);
4. you must segregate and partially release records where possible, §§ 552(a)(8)(A)(ii) and 552(b) (undesignated matter following (b)(9)); and
5. you may not claim deliberative process exemption for records more than 25 years old, § 552(b)(5).


# "Record" defined

For the purposes of this request, except as otherwise specified, "record" means any agreement, appendix, application, assessment, attachment, checklist, circular, contract, correspondence (including but not limited to email), data management plan, documentation of search parameters, email, email attachment, form, guide, handbook, index of records, information consent agreement, information sharing agreement, instruction, interpretation, kit, management instruction, manual, memorandum, memorandum of understanding, notice, notification, opinion, order, plan, policy, policy statement, processing note, publication, recording, referral, report, request certification form, request detail report, response, rule, script, standard operating procedure, submission, talking point, training document, video, or related record described, regardless of publication status.


# Anti-duplication exclusion

This request specifically excludes providing me with new copies of any records which have been already provided to me or published online for free (e.g. on the agency's online "reading room"), in full or identically to the form that would be provided to me under this request (i.e. with exactly the same format, redactions, and claimed exemptions).

This is only an exclusion on providing records under this request that are identical to those already provided to me or available online, and only if I am or have already been provided a link to the online version (if "available online"). 

This exclusion is only intended to limit unnecessary duplication or provision, not to limit what records are responsive to this request, nor to permit failure to disclose the location of a responsive record available online. If this exclusion would in any way increase the cost or duration to respond to this request, it is to be ignored to the extent it does so.

This request is to be treated as separate from all others that I have filed.


# Forwarding; multi-agency / multi-component records

Please forward this request to the FOIA office of every agency component and subcomponent that may have responsive records for independent processing, with a copy to me.

This request includes any records held jointly by your agency in conjunction with any other agency and/or department, in interagency and/or interdepartmental systems of records, or by other agencies or third parties (including contractors) acting pursuant to any agreement with your agency.


# Minimal redaction

Please note that the FOIA requires you to service the maximum extent of my request that can be done via e.g. partial redaction of exempt material. If you believe some portions of a record to be exempt because it contains Sensitive Security Information (SSI,  49 CFR 15 & 1520) or classified information (18 USC 798), please provide a version of the record redacted to the minimum extent necessary to remove exempt information (e.g. per  49 CFR 1520.15), along with adequate information to describe the reason for each specific exemption.


## Redaction of repeatedly occurring content

When redacting any content that appears more than once in the full set of responsive records, please assign a replacement identifier for each, so that your redaction does not obfuscate the commonality.

For example, suppose that responsive records include the names Alice, Bob, Charlie, and Diego, and you determine that each of those names are redactable (e.g. under (b)(7)(C)). Rather than redacting each with only the text "(b)(7)(C)", replace each instance of "Alice" with "(b)(7)(C) - Person 1", each instance of "Bob" with "(b)(7)(C) - Person 2", etc. This e.g. withholds Alice's identity while not withholding the fact of commonality between occurrences.

Please use reasonably descriptive identifiers. For instance, if Elizabeth's name is not redacted but her personal cellphone number is, and that cellphone number appears e.g. both in her email signature and elsewhere by itself, it should in both cases be redacted with the same descriptive identifier, such as "[Alice's cell #]". For documents, this can be specified in the margins. If space or file format does not permit you to do so, then please use a short code (e.g. "[#52]", and provide a table matching codes to full identifiers in your response letter.

If you make any such redactions, please keep but do not provide a table matching codes/identifiers to the redacted content, for use in case your redaction is examined or overturned on appeal or in litigation.

This is a form and format request pertaining to your process of redaction. Because it only applies in situations when you have already exercised the voluntary decision to alter the records from the original form requested, you have necessarily waived any objection to this section "creating a new record", since your act of redaction itself already "makes a new record" in that limited sense. This is only about how you do a redaction you have already decided to make.

This provision limits the scope of your redaction to the minimum possible extent, so that even if you decide to withhold some particular piece of content, you do not also withhold the fact of its being the same as the same content appearing elsewhere. That fact is itself metadata that is explicitly requested as part of this request.

If you decide that the mere fact of two pieces of content being the same is itself withholdable, then please redact it using an identifier that encodes only the reason, and provide a table matching those reason-only identifiers to justifications in your response letter.


# Estimates and rolling updates

In order to help tailor my request, please provide an upfront estimate of the time and cost it will take to complete this request, broken down any significant factors that would affect cost to service, number of records in each category, and your estimate of how many records in the category are likely to be exempt.

Please provide me with incremental updates, with updated estimates for fulfillment of the remainder, rather than having the entirety of the request be blocked until fully completed.


# Form and format; no new records; electronic & original format

Please provide all records in a form and format that gives a unique filename to each distinct record, reflecting the metadata in a reasonably organized fashion, and that the records as produced match the page order (etc) of the original record — so that your cover letters, pincites, withholding claims, etc can be readily understood; the record form and format itself makes clear e.g. what constitutes a distinct record; and the record is comprehensible both internally and with respect to its original context.

Please provide all records in electronic, maximally accessible format, as described below. For paper records, please provide PDF scans as described below. If a responsive record is in electronic format, please provide it in the original electronic format (i.e. as currently stored). If a responsive record is in paper, but the Government also has possession or control of its electronic original, please provide both, with each in the corresponding format.

This request does not ask you to create new records. 

If you determine that a response would require creating a new record that you do not want to create, please first contact me by email with an explanation of what records you have that would most closely match the information requested and might be acceptable substitutes, so that we can reasonably tailor the request.

In particular, I specifically request that you do not create new documents in response to this request that are modifications of a digital record, such as page-view images, print views, scans, or the like. No such creation or substitution is authorized by FOIA or the Privacy Act.

However, if the same or similar records are held in both electronic and paper formats, this request includes both the paper and electronic versions. The paper version and the digital version are distinct records, and each may contain distinct information such as handwritten or other markings on the paper copy and embedded metadata in the electronic version.

I specifically request both the original, electronic format record, and (if it contains any additional markings) the paper record.

To the extent that the native electronic format is proprietary or otherwise not in format accessible by widely available, open source software, I also request
1. an export of the proprietary format into a standard, open format, as described below, and
2. all proprietary software necessary to use and understand the original, proprietary format records.


# Rehab Act § 508 compliance

In accordance with 5 USC 552(a)(3)(B & C) (E-FOIA), Rehabilitation Act § 508, and FOIA IA, I demand that you respond using original, native format, electronic, machine-processable, accessible, open, and well structured records to the maximum extent possible — for both the content of your response, and any communications about the request (such as response letters).

This means, e.g.:
1. native, original format records rather than PDFs or other conversions (see note above re providing both native electronic records and scans of paper records, if both exist);
2. individual files per distinct source record (e.g. one .msg file per email), named clearly using the record's identifier, title, and date, rather than a single file containing multiple concatenated records;
3. records compliant with the Rehabilitation Act § 508, 36 CFR Part 1194, 82 FR 5790, and I​SO 14289­-1;
4. fully digital text records rather than scans, rasterizations, or OCR;
5. complete electronic records, as held on any computer (including phones, servers, backup servers, mail servers, workstations, etc.), including all headers and attachments, fully expanded e-mail addresses, full addresses for address "aliases", full lists for "distribution list" aliases, all embedded and external metadata, complete bitwise digital copies of the original file, all file headers, and all other file content;
6. blackout rather than whiteout redactions, with every redaction marked with all exemption(s) claimed for that redaction;
7. digital redactions rather than black marker or rasterization;
8. lists and structured data as machine-processable spreadsheets (e.g. CSV, SQL, XSL) rather than word documents (e.g. DOC, PDF, TXT, RTF) or partial printouts (e.g. PDF),
9. open format records (e.g. PDF, AVI, MPG) rather than proprietary format records (e.g. WordPerfect, Microsoft Advanced Systems Format (ASF)) (note above re providing both original, proprietary format records and open format records);
10. scans rather than paper copies;
11. digital audio/video files rather than physical tapes;
12. upload to your Electronic Reading Room (or other publicly accessible server) rather than personal transfer (for all items other than the item requesting records related to me or my requests);
13. email or (S)FTP file transfer rather than CD;
14. email correspondence rather than physical mail; etc. 


# Compression, passwords, and uploading large files

Multiple files may be sent in a combined, compressed form using standard ZIP, TAR, GZIP, BZIP2, and/or RAR formats, or sent as separate files, at your discretion.

Do not use any password on any files, including ZIP files etc., unless a password was present in the original, native format (in which case, leave it unaltered, and send me the password).

If there are any files you prefer not to transfer by email (e.g. if they are >10MB), please upload them to me via the link listed below my signature. Doing so is secure, completely free to you, and I will be notified of the upload.


# No physical "duplication"; inspection & direct access

Please note that this request does not request that you physically "duplicate" records, as I do not want you to create any paper or other physical copy for me — I only want electronic versions (or scans, for records that are not fully available in electronic form). As such, I expect there to be no duplication related costs.

Furthermore, I specifically request access for inspection of the records, including direct electronic access, in native format, to any electronic records. 


# Request tracking numbers and estimated completion date

Upon receipt, and in every followup response, please state your tracking number(s) for this request, as well as your specific estimated completion date. 5 USC 552(a)(7).


# Communication about this request and method for responding

If you have any questions or updates about this request, please contact me by email, using only the MuckRock email address from which this request was sent. Please do not send responses to my personal or organizational email addresses unless I specifically request you to do so.

Please ensure that all of your responses comply with § 508 of the Rehabilitation Act, 36 CFR Part 1194, 82 FR 5790, and I​SO 14289­-1. See https://www.access-board.gov/ict/ & https://section508.gov/ .

In particular, please make all correspondence pursuant to this request — including notification and responsive records — by email, with native electronic format records, as specified in the request. I do not authorize you to send anything to me by physical mail unless I specifically state otherwise. 

Do not respond using ZixCorp "Secure Mail" or any other method that "expires" records from being available. Use only actual email and direct attachments, or upload using the link below, unless I explicitly request otherwise.


# "Reasonable description" and tailoring

Please note that a request need only be "reasonably described" in the sense that you understand what is requested and where you can find it. A request is not improper merely because of the amount of responsive records. I will not agree to a limitation premised on this request asking for voluminous records. However, I may agree to a limitation premised on the difficulty of finding particular records or categories thereof, the quality of records available, paper vs electronic format, or similar issues.

If you believe that any of the requested items are not reasonably described, that they would be overly burdensome to fulfill, or that you need any further information, please be specific about what you consider vague. 

Please include in any response about "reasonably described", or any request for narrowing, specific questions I can answer that would clarify matters for you; specific descriptions of what parts of the request more or less burdensome (and why) that could serve as the basis for negotiating a narrower request; and any indexes, finding guides, record categories, record storage practices, likely places that responsive records may be located, or similar information that would allow me to understand your concerns and better tailor the request.


# No fees agreed to; non-commercial status; journalistic & public interest waiver

I am not currently willing to pay for servicing this request. I may be willing to pay if it is necessary; please send a detailed explanation of the costs and their statutory justification, and service the maximum extent of the request that can be done for free in the meantime.

This request is a qualified request for journalistic, public interest purposes. As such, I request fully waived fees, including both public interest fee waiver and journalistic fee waiver.

1. Fiat Fiendum, Inc. (FF) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization, organized for charitable, educational, scientific, and/or literary purposes.

This request is a part of FF's bona fide educational and scientific purpose activities, which are public interest purposes as a matter of law.

2. FF's actions in matters such as this request are non-commercial. My personal interest in the records is also non-commercial.

3. Both Fiat Fiendum as an organization, and I as an individual, are representatives of the news media and entitled to waiver of all search fees.

4. I intend and am able to host and publish all received records online to the general public at no charge, as well to publish highlights, analyses, summaries, commentaries, and other creative, original journalistic and scientific work about responsive records through multiple online publications, as part of Fiat Fiendum's work.

5. The records requested are of significant public interest, entitled to waiver of all duplication fees, since
a. they are requested for 501(c)(3) public interest purposes;
b. as above, I both am able and intend to disseminate the files widely;
c. they would contribute greatly to the public understanding of the operations & activities of your agency, in that they are records that directly describe agency operations & activities, as well as the issues and matters described at the top of this letter; and
d. they are likely to be requested by others.

6. As mentioned above, I am explicitly not asking for any physical duplication, but rather direct server-to-server file transfer or email (or posting on your website). FOIA authorizes "duplication" fees strictly limited to your agency's actual costs, and mandates that your agency use the cheapest available requested methods. I consider the actual costs for server-to-server file transfer to be reasonably estimated by, e.g., Amazon S3's pricing (https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/).

7. I request that, pending fee waiver determination or appeal, you proceed with this request as if it were in the "other non-commercial requester" category.


# Requester

This request is made on behalf of both myself, Sai (in personal capacity) and Fiat Fiendum, Inc. (in official capacity).

“Sai” is my full legal name.

Please note that I am partially blind. I use screen readers (such as VoiceOver and TalkBack). I also need to process documents using computer code (which requires machine-readable data, including metadata). These facts must be considered as part of the basis for, and right to, the form and format requests detailed above.

Sincerely,
Sai
President, Fiat Fiendum, Inc.
Fiat Fiendum is a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt corporation devoted to public interest journalism, government transparency and accountability, individuals' civil rights, and related issues.

Upload link and physical mail address are below. (Again, do not physically mail responsive records without my explicit request; send all responses electronically.)

title: All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under 
the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com), 
exchanged with any Dieringer School District email account, alias, or internal 
routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient, 
carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirety of the District's 
available archival retention window.



TECHNICAL PRE-EXCLUSION OF REPETITIVE SYSTEM DATA:

To maximize administrative processing efficiency, accelerate delivery, and 
eliminate unnecessary review burdens, the requester explicitly waives 
interest in, pre-excludes, and requests the system-level filtering out of 
the following non-substantive records categories:

1. Automated calendar invitations, change notifications, or updates.
2. Automated out-of-office or vacation autoreplies generated by either domain.
3. System-generated IT alerts, ticket confirmations, or password actions.



LIMITATION OF SCOPE & PRE-EXCLUSION OF SENSITIVE DATA:

The requester explicitly pre-excludes and waives any interest in the 
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of any individual student under FERPA.

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.210, if the District asserts that specific internal 
staff names or student indicators are exempt from disclosure, the District is 
required to apply narrow blackouts exclusively to those individual text strings 
while releasing the remaining non-exempt text blocks, financial totals, 
and generalized policy or administrative discussions. 

Blanket withholding of entire records based on broad assertions of privilege 
or exempt status is explicitly contested; only the minimal exempt portions 
may be withheld.



MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:

As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a formal response is required within five (5) 
business days.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

requestor or a representative of the requestor fails to claim or review the
records within the thirty-day period or make other arrangements, the

title: Final Disposition and Aspen Incident No. 2257153 (May 20, 2022–Present)

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: Final Disposition and Aspen Incident No. 2257153 (May 20, 2022–Present)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

I request records dated from May 20, 2022 through the date of your search and response concerning the complaint reported by Nichole Allen on or about May 27, 2022 and its association with Aspen Incident No. 2257153.

For purposes of this request, "disposition" includes any finding, determination, conclusion, resolution, closure decision, administrative outcome, status designation, screening decision, referral decision, or other action reflecting how CPS ultimately handled the complaint.

Please produce:

1. Final Disposition Records

Any investigative report, investigative summary, finding, conclusion, determination, recommendation, disposition, closure record, administrative review, or final outcome record relating to the complaint associated with Aspen Incident No. 2257153.

Any records identifying:

A. the allegations reviewed;
B. the findings reached;
C. the final disposition;
D. the date of closure; and
E. the individual(s) responsible for the final determination.

Any records reflecting that:

A. no investigation was conducted;
B. no findings were made;
C. no disposition was issued; or
D. no closure record was created.

Any record reflecting the final administrative disposition of the complaint, regardless of title, including records reflecting that no disposition or determination was made.

2. Aspen Incident No. 2257153

A. A complete copy of Aspen Incident No. 2257153 as it existed at final disposition or closure, including all narratives, classifications, status fields, disposition fields, closure fields, School-Wide Response entries, witness statements, attachments, supporting documents, and related records.

B. All versions of Aspen Incident No. 2257153, including original, amended, revised, superseded, archived, and final versions.

C. All audit logs, metadata, revision histories, activity logs, change histories, status histories, and system-generated records relating to Incident No. 2257153.

3. All records identifying:

A. who created;
B. edited;
C. modified;
D. eviewed;
F. approved; or
G. closed

Incident No. 2257153, including the date and time of each action.

All records reflecting, documenting, supporting, authorizing, approving, or resulting in the classification of Incident No. 2257153 as an Event Reason of "Discipline."

Any records identifying the disposition code, closure code, resolution category, administrative outcome, or final status assigned to Incident No. 2257153.

3. June 3, 2022 Communications

A. Any records reflecting whether CPS considers the June 3, 2022 emails, School-Wide Response, or Aspen Incident No. 2257153 to constitute the final disposition of the complaint.

B. If CPS contends that the June 3, 2022 communications and/or Aspen Incident No. 2257153 constitute the final disposition of the complaint, please identify the records supporting that determination.

4. Certification of Final Version

If CPS contends that any produced copy of Aspen Incident No. 2257153 is the final version, please certify:

A. that it is the final version;
B. the date it became final;
C. whether modifications were made after June 3, 2022;
D. whether prior versions existed; and
E. whether the produced version is a complete and accurate copy of the final Aspen record relied upon by CPS.

5 If no final disposition record, closure record, investigative conclusion, or administrative outcome record exists, please expressly state that no such record exists.

6. No-Records Certification

If no responsive records exist, please provide a written certification identifying:

A. the offices, custodians, systems, and databases searched;
B. the date range searched;
C. whether responsive records ever existed;
D. whether any responsive records were destroyed, deleted, overwritten, archived, migrated, or purged; and
E. the records-retention schedule governing the requested records.

6. Preservation Notice

A. Because these records may be relevant to administrative, civil-rights, employment, student-protection, special-education, or other proceedings, CPS is requested to take reasonable steps to preserve potentially responsive records pending completion of this request.

B. This includes Aspen records, audit logs, metadata, revision histories, emails, Teams messages, witness statements, uploaded documents, EOCO records, Office of Student Protections records, Safety and Security records, Network records, archived records, and backup records relating to Aspen Incident No. 2257153 or the complaint reported on or about May 27, 2022.


7. If any portion of this request is denied, please identify the records withheld, the statutory exemption relied upon, the factual basis for the denial, and the name and title of the person responsible for the denial as required by 5 ILCS 140/9.

Respectfully,

TINA PEARSON

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Tina Pearson

ISSRA prohibits the disclosure of students and any student records in which a student may be individually identified by a school regardless of how or where the information pursuant to (105 ILCS 10/2(d). Redactions have also been made in accordance with 5 ILCS 140/7(1)(j)(iii) which exempts from release information concerning a school or university’s adjudication of student disciplinary cases, but only to the extent that disclosure would unavoidably reveal the identity of the student. communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: Axon Contract and Procurement Materials
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) is submitting this request for records under the Illinois Freedom of Information Act. related to the acquisition and cost of services and devices provided by Axon and any of its subsidiaries and partners. 

*Background*
Axon (also known as Axon Enterprise, Inc.) is a company that describes itself as providing “public safety technology solutions” to a variety of customers, many of which are law enforcement agencies based in the United States. For reference, Axon’s website is www.axon.com. These “solutions” may be equipment, software, or “artificial intelligence”-driven analysis of video and data. Some examples of equipment, software, and services created and sold by Axon include (but are not limited to):
• the TASER, a conducted energy device
• body-worn cameras (often referred to as “Axon Body”)
• Axon Fusus, a platform used to integrate cameras and other data into a “real-time crime center” (RTCC) 
• Axon 911, an AI-driven assistant platform for dispatchers
• Axon Evidence, a platform to integrate evidence and other information
• Axon Outpost, an automated license plate reader (ALPR) system
• Axon Lightpost, an ALPR system designed for integration with streetlights
• the Axon AI Era Plan, a collection of AI-driven analysis software (www.axon.com/products/axon-ai-era-plan)
• Axon Vision, an AI-driven video analysis system
• Axon Assistant, an AI-driven chatbot
• Axon Draft One, an AI-assisted police report generation feature
• Axon Records, a records management system
• Axon virtual reality training
• Axon Air DFR, a drone-as-first-responder platform, which may also include drones created by a company called Skydio

Axon provides services or devices to the majority of policing agencies in the United States. Axon often “bundles” services and devices into a single contract, makes adjustments and additions to existing agreements for the provision of new goods, and is designated a “sole source provider” during the procurement process. Contracts and agreements may be active for many years and may include “escalator” clauses that describe ongoing and increasing costs for the procurement over the life of the contract.

*Timeframe*
The requested records are all those related to agreements with Axon active during the year 2026, as well as those agreements related to devices, services, and payments to be provided in the future. 

*Requested records*
This public records request is for materials related to the acquisition and cost of services and devices provided by Axon and any of its subsidiaries and partners. 

1. CONTRACT AND AGREEMENTS
All contracts, memorandums of understanding, and any other written agreements between this agency and Axon. Response records included all associated amendments, exhibits, and supplemental and supporting documentation for each agreement, including any amendments and materials generated subsequent to the initial contract agreement. If this agency uses any Axon product, including but not limited to the ones listed above, agreements referencing those products are responsive to this request; this includes all agreements related to “trial” or “free” periods of use. 

2. FINANCIAL AND PROCUREMENT MATERIALS
All relevant procurement and financial documents and agreements, as well as records of financial transactions, exchanges, and obligations relevant to devices and services procured from Axon. Some of these details and documents may be included as part of the Master Services and Purchasing Agreement or related quotes. 
Responsive materials include: 
• quote materials
• invoices and bills
• records describing specific pricing for each associated line item, including the unit price, the quantity procured of each unit, and associated pricing components. If additional products will be procured over the life of the contract, please be sure to provide records that reflect future acquisitions under the agreement and their cost. 
• receipts
• Requests for Proposal to which Axon provided a response
• bidding materials provided by Axon
• justifications for sole source designation (or equivalent designation, if different terminology is used in your jurisdiction) and associated materials. Responsive materials include any letters and drafts provided by Axon, any supporting materials provided by the company, and any related resolutions and materials generated by the jurisdiction in the process of obtaining a sole source designation for Axon. If the company is not subject to competitive purchasing procedures for a reason that is not a “sole source designation” (for example, because the agreement is part of a cooperative or collaborative purchase), please provide records sufficient to show why the company or the contract is not subject to competitive bidding. 
• records sufficient to show the projected ongoing cost of the agreement with Axon
• records reflecting any discounts or other calculations that were figured into the costs associated with this procurement

*Provision of records*
We ask that these materials be provided on a rolling basis; please provide materials to us as your office collects and reviews records. Please contact us for further discussion regarding the search and release of these materials.

*Fees*
In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform us of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. 
This request is not being made for commercial purposes. Please assess fees appropriately in accordance with a public records request being made in the public interest for research and journalism purposes.

*Format of responsive records*
I request that all records be disclosed in their native, digital format and transmitted to us electronically. 

*Contact information*
If you need any more information in order to process the request, or cannot process a portion of the request for any reason, please respond to the email address on this request or “beryl@eff.org”. Please let us know if a phone call will be necessary or desirable; such contact information will be provided upon request.

Thank you very much for your time and help.

Sincerely,
Beryl Lipton

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Andover Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

All contracts, memorandums of understanding, and any other written agreements between this agency and Axon. Response records included all associated amendments, exhibits, and supplemental and supporting documentation for each agreement, including any amendments and materials generated subsequent to the initial contract agreement. If this agency uses any Axon product, including but not limited to the ones listed above, agreements referencing those products are responsive to this request; this includes all agreements related to “trial” or “free” periods of use. 

2. FINANCIAL AND PROCUREMENT MATERIALS
All relevant procurement and financial documents and agreements, as well as records of financial transactions, exchanges, and obligations relevant to devices and services procured from Axon. Some of these details and documents may be included as part of the Master Services and Purchasing Agreement or related quotes. 
Responsive materials include: 
• quote materials
• invoices and bills
• records describing specific pricing for each associated line item, including the unit price, the quantity procured of each unit, and associated pricing components. If additional products will be procured over the life of the contract, please be sure to provide records that reflect future acquisitions under the agreement and their cost. 
• receipts
• Requests for Proposal to which Axon provided a response
• bidding materials provided by Axon
• justifications for sole source designation (or equivalent designation, if different terminology is used in your jurisdiction) and associated materials. Responsive materials include any letters and drafts provided by Axon, any supporting materials provided by the company, and any related resolutions and materials generated by the jurisdiction in the process of obtaining a sole source designation for Axon. If the company is not subject to competitive purchasing procedures for a reason that is not a “sole source designation” (for example, because the agreement is part of a cooperative or collaborative purchase), please provide records sufficient to show why the company or the contract is not subject to competitive bidding. 
• records sufficient to show the projected ongoing cost of the agreement with Axon
• records reflecting any discounts or other calculations that were figured into the costs associated with this procurement

*Provision of records*
We ask that these materials be provided on a rolling basis; please provide materials to us as your office collects and reviews records. Please contact us for further discussion regarding the search and release of these materials.

*Fees*
In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform us of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. 
This request is not being made for commercial purposes. Please assess fees appropriately in accordance with a public records request being made in the public interest for research and journalism purposes.

*Format of responsive records*
I request that all records be disclosed in their native, digital format and transmitted to us electronically. 

*Contact information*
If you need any more information in order to process the request, or cannot process a portion of the request for any reason, please respond to the email address on this request or “beryl@eff.org”. Please let us know if a phone call will be necessary or desirable; such contact information will be provided upon request.

Thank you very much for your time and help.

Sincerely,
Beryl Lipton

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: BPD Officer Earnings 2025-2026
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

This is a public records request pursuant to Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66, § 10A. I hereby request the following records.
I hereby request an excel/CSV extraction containing officer earning data between 07/01/2025 and 06/30/2026:
City of Boston Employee ID (6 digit ID)
Employee first name
Employee last name
Employee middle name
Badge Number
POST ID
Rank
Current Unit
Year
Sex
Regular earnings
Overtime earnings
Detail earnings
Quinn earnings
Retroactive earnings
Other earnings
Total earnings

I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2020) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f).
Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents.
I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.
If you do not waive the fees associated with my request, please provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate and explanation of the fees prior to fulfilling my request. See 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”).
If you believe any of the records I have requested are exempt from disclosure, please identify both: (1) the records, categories of records, or portions of the records you intend to withhold; and (2) the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption you are relying on. See ch. 66, § 10(b)(iv).
If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at (650)-223-1665 or adasuss@bu.edu
Thank you in advance for your time and attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving your response within 10 calendar days. See ch. 66, § 10(a)

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

ada sussman

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

11/1/2026
Dear Records Custodian:

This is a public records request pursuant to Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66, § 10A. I hereby request the following records.

I hereby request an excel/CSV extraction containing records of the following fields of information for all Boston Police Department employees from 8/1/2025 to 9/1/2025. Please include the following fields of information:
 
Employee first name
Employee last name
Employee middle name
Badge Number

I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2025) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f).

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents.

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.

If you do not waive the fees associated with my request, please provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate and explanation of the fees prior to fulfilling my request. See 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”).

If you believe any of the records I have requested are exempt from disclosure, please identify both: (1) the records, categories of records, or portions of the records you intend to withhold; and (2) the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption you are relying on. See ch. 66, § 10(b)(iv).

If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at (475)-243-3786 and mchristi@bu.edu

Thank you in advance for your time and attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving your response within 10 calendar days. See ch. 66, § 10(a).

Sincerely,
Michael Christie
BU SPARK!

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

ada sussman

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

11/1/2026
Dear Records Custodian:

This is a public records request pursuant to Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66, § 10A. I hereby request the following records.

I hereby request an excel/CSV extraction containing records of the following fields of information for all Boston Police Department employees from 12/1/2024 to 1/1/2025. Please include the following fields of information:
 
Employee first name
Employee last name
Employee middle name
Badge Number

I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2021) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f).

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents.

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.

If you do not waive the fees associated with my request, please provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate and explanation of the fees prior to fulfilling my request. See 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”).

If you believe any of the records I have requested are exempt from disclosure, please identify both: (1) the records, categories of records, or portions of the records you intend to withhold; and (2) the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption you are relying on. See ch. 66, § 10(b)(iv).

If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at (475)-243-3786 and mchristi@bu.edu

Thank you in advance for your time and attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving your response within 10 calendar days. See ch. 66, § 10(a).

Sincerely,
Michael Christie
BU SPARK!

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

ada sussman

This is a public records request pursuant to Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66, § 10A. I hereby request the following records.

Employee first name
Employee last name
Employee middle name
Badge Number

Michael Christie

ada sussman

Employee last name
Employee middle name
Badge Number

I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2024) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f).

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents.

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.

Sincerely,
Michael Christie

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

ada sussman
